title: The Promise Stands
subtitle: The Hour is not a possibility. It is an appointment.
sources: Qur'an 33:63 — 'People ask you concerning the Hour. Say, Knowledge of it is only with Allah'
Qur'an 20:15 — 'Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6503 — the Prophet ﷺ held up two fingers: he was sent and the Hour is near (narrated by Sahl)
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the ten signs before the Hour (Hudhayfa ibn Asid)

chapters.heading: Almost Concealed
chapters.body: The Qur'an states the end of the world the way calendars state the seasons — as settled fact: 'Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives' (20:15). Almost concealed: close enough to shape every choice, far enough that no one builds a business on the date. The Prophet ﷺ held up two fingers and said that he was sent and the Hour is near, like these two (Sahih al-Bukhari 6503) — and Sahih Muslim 2901 reports that the Hour will not come until ten signs are seen, each a catastrophe with a name. The mercy of the design is in the concealment: had the date been known, the last generation would inherit everything and earn nothing; had it been deniable, no one would prepare. So it stays almost — the appointment on the wall with no hour beneath it, and the entire art of faith is living ready for a knock that has no schedule.

familyQuestion: The date is hidden but the appointment is certain. How would you spend this week if the knock came Friday?

title: The Moon Split
subtitle: The first great sign the Qur'an itself named
sources: Qur'an 54:1-2 — 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3637 — the people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign and he showed them the splitting of the moon (Anas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3636 — the moon was split in two in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, and he said 'Bear witness' (Ibn Mas'ud)

chapters.heading: And They Saw It
chapters.body: The Qur'an opens Surah Al-Qamar with it: 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]. And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, Passing magic' (54:1-2). Anas reports that the people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ to show them a sign, and he showed them the moon split (Sahih al-Bukhari 3637); Ibn Mas'ud reports that the moon was split in two in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime and that he said, bear witness (Sahih al-Bukhari 3636). The verse names what followed: they called it passing magic. The verse frames denial not as ignorance of the sign, but as refusal of its meaning. A miracle is not evidence for those committed to unbelief; the moon can split and the witness can shrug. Signs ask something of the heart before they ask anything of the eyes.

familyQuestion: They saw the moon split and called it magic. What have you seen with your own eyes that you're explaining away?

title: The Minor Signs
subtitle: The syllabus of the centuries — read as milestones, not dates
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1036 — signs: knowledge lost, quakes, time shortens (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 80 — knowledge taken away with the learned, ignorance established, wine drunk widely, open fornication (Anas)
Sahih Muslim 8 — the hadith of Jibril: among the signs of the Hour, barefoot destitute herders competing in tall buildings
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2210 — signs of trial (da'if per Darussalam)
Qur'an 81:1-14 — the surah of the falling signs

chapters.heading: Knowledge Lifted
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ mapped the centuries in single sentences, and the hadith collections preserve the map: time will shorten (Sahih al-Bukhari 1036); knowledge will be taken away with the death of the learned and ignorance will become established, wine will be drunk widely and open fornication will spread (Sahih al-Bukhari 80); barefoot, destitute herders will compete in constructing tall buildings (Sahih Muslim 8); a man will obey his wife and disobey his mother, and treat his friend well and abandon his father (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2210, da'if per Darussalam). Each generation has read the list and seen its own decade in it — which is precisely the design: the signs are not a countdown but a curriculum, issued so that every century would find its warnings addressed to it personally. The minor signs end where Surah At-Takwir ends: 'So where are you going? It is not except a reminder to the worlds' (81:26-27). The signs are not there to date the Hour. They are there to wake the sleeper.

familyQuestion: Every generation found its own decade in the list. Which lines describe your decade most exactly?

title: The Ten Major Signs
subtitle: The ten signs named in the hadith — the report does not fix their order
sources: Sahih Muslim 2901 — the ten signs (Hudhayfa ibn Asid): the Smoke, the Dajjal, the Beast, the sunrise from the west, the descent of Isa, Ya'juj and Ma'juj, three sinkings, and a fire driving people to their place of assembly (the report does not say that this is the order in which they occur)

chapters.heading: One After Another
chapters.body: The hadith of Hudhayfa ibn Asid says the Hour will not come until ten signs are seen (Sahih Muslim 2901). It lists them as: the Smoke; the Dajjal; the Beast; the sunrise from the west; the descent of Isa son of Maryam; Ya'juj and Ma'juj; three great sinkings of the earth — one in the east, one in the west and one in Arabia; and, last of them, a fire from the Yemen that drives people to the place of their assembly. The report does not say that the signs happen in the order it lists them, so this card does not claim one. Take the comfort that is in the list: it holds the Dajjal, and it also holds the descent of Isa son of Maryam; and it ends with the fire that drives people to the gathering for judgment itself.

familyQuestion: The hadith names ten signs and gives no calendar. If the order is not given to you, what should you do about being ready today?

title: The Smoke
subtitle: A visible smoke that covers the people
sources: Qur'an 44:10-11 — 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. Covering the people; this is a painful torment'
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the Smoke among the ten signs

chapters.heading: A Smoke Over the People
chapters.body: 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. Covering the people; this is a painful torment' (44:10-11). The Smoke is the first sign in the list of ten in Sahih Muslim 2901. Reports about how it affects the believer and the disbeliever, and how long it lasts, are not told here. As a reflection: a sign is a warning, and a warning is a mercy only to the one who acts on it. The Hour's signs don't create the two kinds of people. They simply stop letting them hide from the difference.

familyQuestion: The smoke is a sign that covers everyone. What warning are you hearing now that you could act on before it has to be repeated louder?

title: The Beast
subtitle: A creature that speaks from the earth
sources: Qur'an 27:82 — 'And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them'
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the Beast among the ten signs
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3187 — what the Beast does (da'if per Darussalam; al-Tirmidhi himself called it hasan)

chapters.heading: The Earth's Witness
chapters.body: 'And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith]' (27:82). The Beast is among the ten signs in Sahih Muslim 2901. Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3187 (da'if per Darussalam; al-Tirmidhi himself called it hasan) reports that it comes out of the earth with the ring of Sulayman and the staff of Musa, brightens the faces of the believers and marks the noses of the disbelievers with the ring, so that at a gathering one is addressed as 'believer' and the other as 'disbeliever'. Because Darussalam grades that report weak, it is mentioned with that caveat. The Qur'an's own phrasing is the lesson: the Beast 'speaks to them' — the earth itself becomes a witness when the people would not hear the prophets. It comes, in the verse's words, when the word befalls them. Some hearts only understand when the ground they stood on rises and speaks.

familyQuestion: The earth itself will testify. What is the ground of your life saying about you right now — before it has to speak?

title: The Sun Rises from the West
subtitle: The sign after which faith no longer helps one who had not believed before
sources: Qur'an 6:158 — 'The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good'
Sahih al-Bukhari 4635 — the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west; when people see it all will believe, and it will not benefit a soul that had not believed before (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the sunrise from the west among the ten signs

chapters.heading: When Seeing Stops Counting
chapters.body: The order of nature is the last argument: 'The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good' (6:158). Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west; when people see it, everyone on the earth will believe — and that is when, as the hadith has it, believing does a soul no good if it had not believed before (Sahih al-Bukhari 4635). The sunrise from the west is also among the ten signs of Sahih Muslim 2901. Read together, every sign before this one is a summons, and this one is the deadline — after it, seeing is believing and believing no longer avails, because the trial was built for the unseen. 'And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude' (25:62) — the alternation itself was the proof, repeated every twenty-four hours, free of charge, for a lifetime. The sunrise will simply be the morning the proof stops being subtle.

familyQuestion: The sun rises from the west only when it's too late. What are you treating as 'too subtle' that is actually your daily proof?

title: The Forty Days of the Dajjal
subtitle: Forty days that test every soul alive
sources: Sahih Muslim 2937 — the Dajjal's itinerary: forty days, one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, the rest like your days
Sahih al-Bukhari, number not re-checked — 'there was no prophet but he warned his people'

chapters.heading: Forty Days of Fire and Rain
chapters.body: The hadith draws the forty days in detail: the Dajjal stays forty days — one day like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and the rest like your days — and he travels every highway except Makkah and Madinah, which the angels turn him from; with him is a garden and a fire, and his fire is coolness and his garden is flame (Muslim 2937). His temptations are not crude: he brings provision to those who follow him and famine to those who refuse — the economics of obedience inverted, as if the whole test of life were run in forty accelerated days. And the Prophet ﷺ said: since the creation of Adam there has been no fitnah like the fitnah of the Dajjal (Muslim 2946) — the concentration of every trial humanity has ever known, compressed into one figure, for forty days. The exit was given before the trial was: al-Kahf's first and last verses, memorized before his arrival, and the Prophet ﷺ said: he will not harm whoever recites them (Muslim, number not re-checked). The greatest test in history came with its answer key, published fourteen centuries early.

familyQuestion: The greatest trial came with its answer key. Do you know the first and last verses of al-Kahf by heart yet?

title: The Descent of Isa
subtitle: The return the prophets promised and the Qur'an sealed
sources: Qur'an 4:157-159 — 'And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death'
Sahih al-Bukhari 2476 — the descent, the cross broken, the Qur'an ruling
Sahih Muslim 2937 — Isa kills the Dajjal at the gate of Ludd

chapters.heading: He Descends at the White Minaret
chapters.body: The hadith fixes the scene: Isa son of Maryam descends at the white minaret in the eastern part of the Damascus mosque, his hands resting on the wings of two angels (Muslim 2937). He comes not to begin a new revelation but to complete this one: he breaks the cross, kills the swine, abolishes the jizyah — no one left to pay it, all either believing or perishing — and rules by this Qur'an as a Muslim among Muslims (Bukhari 2476), praying behind a leader from among the Muslims — the report does not name that leader. His first act of judgment is the Dajjal's end: at the gate of Ludd in Palestine, Isa catches him, and the narration says the Dajjal melts like salt in water at the sight of him — or dissolves by Isa's spear (Muslim 2937). The Qur'an sealed the theology in advance: 'And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness' (4:159). The world's longest argument ends with the living Witness standing among them.

familyQuestion: Isa returns to rule by the Qur'an. What does it mean that every road in history ends at the same Book?

title: Ya'juj and Ma'juj Released
subtitle: The wall stands by decree; the release is scheduled
sources: Qur'an 18:98 — 'when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level'
Qur'an 21:96-97 — 'from every elevation, descend And [when] the true promise has approached'

chapters.heading: Level Ground
chapters.body: 'Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend And [when] the true promise has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring' (21:96-97). The hadith fills the release with sound: every day the hordes tunnel at the wall, and every evening their leader says: come back tomorrow — and each day the tunnel is restored, until the day he says — in Allah's name, we will finish it tomorrow — and returns to find the wall like it was (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3153 — hasan gharib per al-Tirmidhi, sahih per Darussalam; Sunan Ibn Majah 4080 — sahih per Darussalam). Ibn Kathir, as reported by Ma'ariful Qur'an, doubted that this report goes back to the Prophet ﷺ; see Go deeper. The sentence history repeats in al-Kahf's daily recitation — 'but when the promise of my Lord comes' (18:98) — becomes the event. Their surge, the tradition says, drains Lake Tiberias; Isa and the believers withdraw to Mount Tur; and the ending is sudden and strange: Allah sends a worm in their necks, and by morning they are all dead — a nation that terrified the world dies in one night by the smallest of creatures (Muslim 2937). The loudest trial in the sequence ends in silence.

familyQuestion: A nation that terrified the world died in one night by a worm. What giant in your life is smaller than it looks?

title: The Fire
subtitle: A fire, and the gathering
sources: Sahih Muslim 2901 — the last of the ten signs: a fire from the Yemen driving people to their place of assembly
Qur'an 50:42 — 'The Day they will hear the blast [of the Horn] in truth'
Qur'an 39:68-69 — the two blasts and the earth shining with its Lord's light

chapters.heading: A Fire to the Gathering
chapters.body: The last of the ten signs in Sahih Muslim 2901 is a fire that comes out of the Yemen and drives people to the place of their assembly. This card does not try to describe anything beyond what that report says. Then, in the Qur'an, the silence: 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills' (39:68). And after the silence, the second blast: 'and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51). The fire that gathers them is the last sign because it delivers them to the appointment itself — the plain where, the Qur'an says, 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth' (39:69).

familyQuestion: The gathering is the last sign because it's the first moment of the meeting. Ready or not — what's your status?

title: The End of the Story
subtitle: The kingdom that never ends
sources: Qur'an 39:69-70 — 'and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged'
Qur'an 21:104 — 'The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records'
Qur'an 98:8 — 'Their reward with Allah will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow'

chapters.heading: Folding the Sky
chapters.body: The Qur'an ends the world the way a scribe ends a scroll: 'The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Then the judgment: 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged' (39:69). And then the story that outlasts the sky itself opens: 'Their reward with Allah will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord' (98:8). The Last Day is not the end of the story; it is the end of the chapter titled *Trial*. The book it opens has no final page — 'a promise binding upon Us; indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Every sign in this shelf exists to make that page reachable.

familyQuestion: The world ends like a folded scroll — and the next book has no last page. Which book are you writing your page for right now?
